test_name: kuna-analysis entry recall, decbench ARM Cortex-M corpus (16 binaries x 3 opt levels, 41378 DWARF entries)
inspiration: decbench:O2-cleanflight-cleanflight_DALRCF405, O2-betaflight-betaflight_STM32F405, O2-crazyflie-cf2, O2-nuttx-nuttx; kuna's own ARM entry-recall measurement (docs/features/cortexmvectors/analysis.md; step 1 of the arm-entry-granularity proposal)

decisions.question: Does the widening need a named option, or is it a strict bug fix?
decisions.answer: Option. It discovers more functions, so it changes emitted C by construction — it is not a case of wrong output being corrected. Gated per the repo rule; default-OFF.

decisions.question: Where does the flag get read?
decisions.answer: A standalone CortexMVectorsPass (id `cortexmvectors`), stashed at load and gated at commit by engine.rs::analysis_pass_enabled — the eh_frame_full/funcstart_patterns shape. Reading arch.analysis_cortexmvectors inside EntryDiscoveryPass::run was tried and silently did nothing, because load-time passes run before `--option` is applied.

decisions.question: Should the widened handlers also seed the Listing walk and paint its ContextPainter?
decisions.answer: No, measured. Entries+paints only: +96 GT, 81.4% precision, 0 lost. Plus the walk's region paint: +86, 73.8%, 10 GT lost. Plus walk seeds: +44, 74.2%, 54 GT lost. The walk treats an unconditional B as same-function flow, so an ISR stub that tail-calls a shared handler absorbs it and the handler's own entry fails code_pointer_table_seeds' is_undefined guard. That is proposal step 3's tail-call split; until it lands the conservative wiring wins on every axis.

decisions.question: What replaces `word[1] == e_entry` without inviting false positives?
decisions.answer: A run of >= 3 Thumb handler pointers (odd, in an executable section), counted over accepted SLOTS not distinct addresses — a bare-metal table aims most vectors at one shared Default_Handler, so distinct addresses undercount badly. Measured: no allocated section in the 16-binary corpus reaches three except the real table, including cleanflight's .text whose first word accidentally lands in the SRAM window.

decisions.question: Why no tests/stages/*.xml two-pass case?
decisions.answer: The oracle keys entirely on ELF structure (sh_flags, PT_LOAD flags, e_entry, section bytes at a section base). The datatest harness embeds raw bytechunks and never constructs an ObjectLoadImage, so the option is unobservable there. Replaced by kuna-console/tests/verify_cortexmvectors.rs, a two-pass cross-crate gate over a committed fixture — the same wiring every sibling analysis-tier discovery flag uses.
